title: Auto Loans: Posted-Balance Limit on Transfers from Checking
content:
When PCB pays an Auto Loans installment by drawing on the borrower's PCB checking account, only money already posted to that account can be used.

## Rule

Money is drawn from the checking account that the borrower holds in active status, and the posted money available there is that account's ledger balance. The payment drawn is set against the sum still owed on the installment:

- where the ledger balance is lower than that sum, the payment drawn is the ledger balance;
- in every other case, the payment drawn is the sum still owed.

The payment is stated to the cent. A borrower with no active checking account has no posted money to draw on. The payment settled here is the figure from which its whole division into fees, interest and principal is then made.

## Decision table

| Ledger balance of the active checking account, set against the sum still owed | Payment drawn |
|---|---|
| lower | the ledger balance |
| equal | the sum still owed (the two coincide) |
| higher | the sum still owed |

## Examples (invented balances)

- Still owed 312.00, ledger balance 280.40: the payment drawn is 280.40, and the installment stays partly unpaid.
- Still owed 312.00, ledger balance 1900.00: the payment drawn is 312.00.
- Still owed 312.00, ledger balance exactly 312.00: the payment drawn is 312.00.
